title: Topological invariance
statement:
For a finite universal homeomorphism $r:X\to Y$,
pullback is an equivalence
$r^*:D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)\simeq D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ (the categories of
[def-trf-coefficient-conventions]), with inverse $Rr_*=Rr_!$ and
invertible unit and counit. This includes reduction.

proof.text: Work throughout in the finite-coefficient and geometric setting of [def-trf-coefficient-conventions]: $A=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$, $n\geq1$, $\ell\ne p$, and $X,Y$ are separated finite-type schemes over $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, with $r$ a $k$-morphism. These are the geometric schemes and coefficient categories named in [sk-d-setup]. Apply [lem-trf-proetale-topological-invariance] to the given universal homeomorphism. Its unit and counit on sheaves of sets are isomorphisms. This is the pro-etale site input required here; the opening etale-site argument of the blueprint alone concerns etale sheaves, whereas the coefficient categories in the statement are pro-etale categories.

source.place: Tag 09AB (lemma-thickening); blueprint proof, opening site-equivalence sentences

proof.text: Lift this equivalence to constant-$A$ module sheaves. Apply $r^{-1}$ to the addition and action maps and transport the coefficient action through $c_A:r^{-1}A_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}A_X$, the isomorphism of [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map]. Naturality of the set-sheaf unit and counit with respect to addition, zero and the action map makes both maps $A$-linear, so they remain inverse isomorphisms in the module categories. This gives $r^*\dashv r_*$ as an equivalence on module sheaves. The pullback is exactly the exact functor of [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact]. Its inverse $r_*$ is exact as well: an equivalence preserves the universal properties of kernels and cokernels.

source.place: Exact inverse/direct images paragraph; constant-ring module action written out

proof.text: Apply these two exact functors degree by degree to cochain complexes. Exactness preserves the kernel, image and quotient defining cohomology, and therefore gives $H^i(r^*C)=r^*H^i(C)$ and $H^i(r_*C)=r_*H^i(C)$, so both preserve quasi-isomorphisms. By the localization definition [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], their termwise unit and counit descend to inverse isomorphisms on derived categories; the triangle equations descend too. The finite-level definition [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] identifies this termwise pullback with $Lr^*$. For a K-injective resolution $C\to I$, exactness of $r_*$ makes $r_*C\to r_*I$ a quasi-isomorphism, identifying termwise $r_*$ with $Rr_*$ as defined in [def-weil-derived-direct-image]. Thus the canonical derived adjunction has invertible unit and counit.

source.place: Derived-category passage: replace the injective-resolution sentence by explicit exact-functor localization

proof.text: Since $r$ is finite, it is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-proper]; in particular it is separated and of finite type by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Hence clauses (i) and (iii) of [thm-sf-ctf-stability] apply over the same algebraically closed field and with the same finite ring $A$. They show respectively that $Lr^*$ and $Rr_*$ carry the indicated bounded constructible finite-Tor subcategories into each other. Restrict the two functors and the unit and counit of the preceding step to these full subcategories. Their triangle identities and invertibility remain valid there. This proves the asserted equivalence on $D^b_{ctf}$ without asserting that every bounded constructible finite-coefficient complex has finite Tor amplitude.

source.place: Constructibility and finite-Tor preservation sentence; use the existing preservation clauses on their exact domains

proof.text: The notation for the derived operations and proper comparison is that of [sk-d-six]; here its comparison is instantiated by the finite-coefficient theorem. For the proper morphism $r$, clause (3) of [prop-functor-package] supplies the canonical isomorphism $\alpha:Rr_!\xrightarrow{\sim}Rr_*$. Write $F=r^*$, $G=Rr_*$ and $H=Rr_!$, with the preceding unit $\eta:1\to GF$ and counit $\varepsilon:FG\to1$. Define $\eta^H_K=\alpha^{-1}_{FK}\circ\eta_K$ and $\varepsilon^H_L=\varepsilon_L\circ F(\alpha_L)$. Both maps are isomorphisms. Naturality of $\alpha$ gives $\varepsilon^H_{FK}\circ F(\eta^H_K)=\varepsilon_{FK}\circ F(\eta_K)=1_{FK}$ and $H(\varepsilon^H_L)\circ\eta^H_{HL}=\alpha_L^{-1}\circ G(\varepsilon_L)\circ\eta_{GL}\circ\alpha_L=1_{HL}$. Hence $Rr_!$ is also a quasi-inverse with invertible unit and counit.

source.place: Sentence Rr_* = Rr_! because r is finite, hence proper

proof.text: For reduction, [lem-weil-pbc-reduction-universal-homeomorphism] states that $i:Y_{\mathrm{red}}\to Y$ is a surjective closed immersion and a universal homeomorphism. By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-finite] it is finite. The reduced closed subscheme is again separated and finite type over $k$: a finite affine cover $Y=\bigcup\operatorname{Spec}B_j$ restricts to $\operatorname{Spec}(B_j/\sqrt{0})$, whose $k$-algebras are generated by the images of any generators of $B_j$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-closed-immersion]. Its diagonal is the base change of the closed diagonal of $Y$ to $Y_{\mathrm{red}}\times_kY_{\mathrm{red}}$ (on affines $(B/I)\otimes_B(B/I)=B/I$); it is closed by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change], so separatedness follows from [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Apply the preceding steps with $r=i$. This proves the reduction clause; no assertion that the nilradical is finitely generated or nilpotent is needed.

proof_origin.place: Entire proof, expanded using Stacks Tag 09AB for the pro-etale input and the existing finite-Tor preservation theorems
